destination.title: String vacua: construction, control and ensembles
destination.question: How can string and related effective-theory vacua be constructed, controlled, counted and analyzed, and what can their distributions and dynamics tell us about low-energy physics?
destination.summary: A proposed navigational family with distinct construction, statistical, computational, phenomenological and geometric directions. Adjacent questions retain alternate homes. This authored scope requires later independent review.

regimes: Source-specific dimensions, supersymmetry conditions, perturbative orders and compactification sectors
assumptions: String embedding, control, finiteness and cosmological selection remain questions where the sources present them as such.
conventions: Discrete counts, signed indices, connected-component bounds, metric volumes and numerical endpoints remain distinct.
No common sampling measure or supersymmetry diagnostic is imposed.
includes: Useful effective-theory and geometric boundary questions
excludes: An asserted universal vacuum construction or selection mechanism
Automatic equivalence of questions sharing an overview card
Universal finiteness inferred from a restricted ensemble or geometric volume

sources.title: Lectures on constructing string vacua

evidence.text: How can approximate, controlled string vacua suitable for phenomenological model building be constructed and analyzed, especially IIB/F-theory flux compactifications with stabilized moduli, and what obstructs control?

sources.title: Field dynamics and tunneling in a flux landscape

evidence.text: How are flux vacua continuously connected, what classical moduli dynamics occurs between them, and what gravitational tunneling processes and rates arise in an explicit Type IIB flux landscape?

sources.title: Seeing through the String Landscape - a String Hunter's Companion in Particle Physics and Cosmology

evidence.text: How can top-down consistency, bottom-up Standard Model construction, landscape statistics and particle/cosmological signatures make classes of string vacua predictive? This is a review spanning intersecting branes, flux stabilization, domain walls and inflation.

sources.title: Some Physical Consequences of an Exact Vacua Distribution in the Bousso-Polchinski Landscape

evidence.text: How can lattice vacua in very thin cosmological-constant shells be counted beyond the Bousso–Polchinski volume approximation, and what does the resulting distribution imply for flux occupation, the smallest positive cosmological constant and possible moduli-stabilization difficulties?

sources.title: Restrictions on infinite sequences of type IIB vacua

evidence.text: Can infinitely many distinct ISD flux vacua accumulate at degeneration limits, particularly the large-complex-structure point approached by previously reported vacuum sequences?

sources.title: Low energy supersymmetry from R-symmetries

evidence.text: When does a continuous or discrete R-symmetry provide a sufficient condition for a supersymmetric vacuum with W = 0, allowing arbitrary field R-charges, and how can this condition be realized in Type IIB flux compactifications?

sources.title: Models of Particle Physics from Type IIB String Theory and F-theory: A Review

evidence.text: Which tools and constructions in type IIB string theory and F-theory can combine moduli stabilization, supersymmetry breaking, chiral matter and realistic interactions into particle-physics vacua?

sources.title: The Noether-Lefschetz problem and gauge-group-resolved landscapes: F-theory on K3  $\times$  K3 as a test case

evidence.text: How can F-theory flux vacua be counted while retaining gauge-group and other algebraic information, correctly identifying equivalent elliptic fibrations and relating discrete Noether–Lefschetz enumeration to continuous vacuum statistics?

sources.title: Genetic Algorithms and the Search for Viable String Vacua

evidence.text: Can genetic algorithms find heterotic string vacua satisfying several discrete phenomenological requirements substantially faster than randomized searches, and can their convergence provide indirect information about structure in the encoded landscape?

sources.title: Type IIA Flux Vacua with Mobile D6-branes

evidence.text: Can classical type IIA flux vacua retain a positive semidefinite potential and non-supersymmetric Minkowski minima when mobile D6-branes mix open and closed moduli, and what supersymmetry-breaking and soft-term patterns follow?

sources.title: Testing Swampland Conjectures with Machine Learning

evidence.text: Can discrete flux patterns explain small vacuum energy within a perturbative compactification and organize spectra compatible with proposed quantum-gravity restrictions?

sources.title: Obstacles to Constructing de Sitter Space in String Theory

evidence.text: When does a candidate flux vacuum belong to a controllable approximation? The paper requires a family of discrete flux choices along which the relevant expansion parameters become small, rather than favorable values at one isolated stationary point.

sources.title: A gravitino distance conjecture

evidence.text: Which asymptotic type IIA vacuum families can be studied using a fixed two-modulus growth sector while retaining large volume and weak coupling?

sources.title: Exponentially Small Cosmological Constant in String Theory

evidence.text: Can quantized data in a string compactification generate vacuum energy below 10^−123 M_pl^4 and extreme separation between the compactification radius and spacetime curvature radius, without an exhaustive search through exponentially many flux choices?

sources.title: Moduli stabilization in asymptotic flux compactifications

evidence.text: How can flux vacua be studied systematically near different boundaries of complex-structure moduli space, rather than by solving a separate transcendental problem for every compactification?

sources.title: Flux vacua of the mirror octic

evidence.text: Can one explicitly enumerate all flux vacua at bounded flux number across the entire moduli space of a concrete type IIB orientifold, rather than sample fluxes or restrict to a boundary region?

sources.title: Moduli Stabilization in String Theory

evidence.text: How can string compactifications yield isolated four-dimensional vacua with massive moduli and broken supersymmetry, while retaining computational control and supporting realistic cosmology and particle physics?

sources.title: Finiteness theorems and counting conjectures for the flux landscape

evidence.text: For a fixed Calabi–Yau fourfold family and tadpole bound, are integral flux-vacuum loci finite in connected components, including near moduli-space boundaries? What further bounds govern their counting, complexity and dimension?

sources.title: Connecting flux vacua through scalar field excursions

evidence.text: Can flux vacua with different integer fluxes become critical points of one scalar potential after integrating in open-string fields, permitting scalar-metric distances and tests of exponential tower-mass decay?

sources.title: An index for flux vacua

evidence.text: Can boundary or asymptotic information about a scalar potential establish the existence of interior critical points, and can an index of DW establish supersymmetric flux vacua?

sources.title: String geometry phenomenology

evidence.text: Can the proposed string-geometry potential select parameters within a restricted nonsupersymmetric heterotic compactification family, and thereby constrain flux quanta, generation number and compactification scale?

sources.title: Counting flux vacua

evidence.text: How many duality-inequivalent supersymmetric flux vacua occur in type IIB Calabi–Yau compactification, how are they distributed, and under what conditions are their numbers finite and approximable by a signed geometric index?

sources.title: Distributions of flux vacua

evidence.text: Determine counts and distributions of supersymmetric and nonsupersymmetric flux vacua over moduli, cosmological constant and supersymmetry-breaking parameters, including the validity of smooth approximations to quantized-flux counts.

sources.title: On the taxonomy of flux vacua

evidence.text: Do explicit integral-flux solutions support the predicted curvature-dependent distribution of IIB no-scale vacua, and how does their number scale with the allowed flux D3 charge L?

sources.title: On the explicit construction and statistics of Calabi-Yau flux vacua

evidence.text: Do explicit type IIB flux vacua in a two-complex-structure-modulus sector follow the Ashok–Douglas index density, and how do their locations, flux charges, axiodilaton values and supersymmetry-breaking scales distribute?

sources.title: Enumerating flux vacua with enhanced symmetries

evidence.text: How frequently do tree-level W=0 vacua and enhanced discrete symmetries occur in tractable IIB flux models, and how do their counts and moduli distributions depend on the D3-charge bound L?

sources.title: R symmetries in the landscape

evidence.text: How severely does preserving a discrete R symmetry restrict flux choices in surveyed IIB compactifications, when do such configurations preserve supersymmetry classically, and how does their abundance differ from R-parity-preserving configurations?

sources.title: A Review of distributions on the string landscape

evidence.text: How can distributions in controllable string-vacuum ensembles guide phenomenological model building? How do finiteness, accumulation points and correlations among viable vacua affect predictivity?

sources.title: A Finite landscape?

evidence.text: Is the number of phenomenologically admissible four-dimensional string/M-theory vacua finite, despite potentially infinite choices of compactification topology, field configurations and fluxes?

sources.title: Generalized Flux Vacua

evidence.text: Which supersymmetric vacua arise in the generalized-flux four-dimensional theory, can their coupling and cosmological constant be tuned, and does their apparent accumulation challenge landscape finiteness?

sources.title: Lectures on constructing string vacua

evidence.text: Flux analysis uses harmonic representatives, Hodge decomposition, Lefschetz SU(2), and periods of the holomorphic four-form. The dimensionless GVW superpotential is W = ℓ_M⁻³∫G₄∧Ω₄; its Kähler-covariant derivatives constrain complex structure.

sources.title: Field dynamics and tunneling in a flux landscape

evidence.text: Use locally inertial coordinates and quadratic Hessian symmetries near extrema to constrain Euclidean paths. For the HM-connected class, the stated single-pass CDL criterion is |λᵢ|>4ε²VN(HM) along a negative-eigenvalue symmetry direction; other weak-gravity classes are not excluded.

sources.title: Seeing through the String Landscape - a String Hunter's Companion in Particle Physics and Cosmology

evidence.text: Open-string disk correlators reduce to Euler Beta functions; their pole expansions organize Regge exchange. Collider estimates broaden resonances with Breit–Wigner widths and combine partonic processes with parton distributions.

sources.title: Some Physical Consequences of an Exact Vacua Distribution in the Bousso-Polchinski Landscape

evidence.text: For equal charges, constructs the occupation distribution by selecting αJ nonzero components with a binomial factor and using θ(q²s)−1 in the contour exponent. The peak is evaluated by saddle methods or statistical sampling; low-dimensional brute-force data are used to assess the minimum-Λ estimate.

sources.title: Restrictions on infinite sequences of type IIB vacua

evidence.text: Refine the Ashok–Douglas argument using the bounded positive quadratic form N̂·(Gτ⊗Gz)·N̂ᵀ=L≤Lmax. Period expansions determine asymptotic eigenvalues and eigenvectors; positivity and flux integrality constrain which components can survive near a D-limit.

sources.title: Low energy supersymmetry from R-symmetries

evidence.text: Write W = sum_i X_i f_i(Y) + W1. R-symmetry forces every term of W1 to contain a quadratic factor A_i A_j or X_i X_j, including nonrenormalizable terms. Setting X = A = 0 kills W1 and its first derivatives; the remaining equations are f_i(Y) = 0.

sources.title: Finiteness of Flux Vacua from Geometric Transitions

evidence.text: What gauge-theory mechanism explains finiteness of supersymmetric flux vacua near local Calabi–Yau singularities, including conifold and Argyres–Douglas degenerations?

sources.title: Four-dimensional String Compactifications with D-Branes, Orientifolds and Fluxes

evidence.text: Which technical tools construct chiral four-dimensional orientifold vacua approaching the supersymmetric Standard Model, determine their effective actions, and support statistical approaches to the vacuum problem? This is a pedagogical review.

sources.title: Asymptotic Flux Compactifications and the Swampland

evidence.text: Do restrictions on flux vacua and axion dynamics survive beyond weak coupling and large volume? The paper approaches this question through four-form flux potentials near boundaries of Calabi–Yau complex-structure moduli space, including boundaries at finite distance.

sources.title: Flux compactification

evidence.text: How can flux compactification stabilize moduli and produce long-lived candidate vacua with broken supersymmetry and small positive cosmological constant, and what can their abundance and distribution imply for observable physics?

sources.title: D-brane Deconstructions in IIB Orientifolds

evidence.text: How can one systematically compute globally consistent D7-brane charges, deformation moduli, flux lattices, gauge groups and matter, and construct worldvolume-flux vacua when generic orientifold D7 worldvolumes are singular?

sources.title: Flux vacua with approximate flat directions

evidence.text: Can quantized flux choices produce type IIB vacua with approximate flat directions beyond constructions requiring a homogeneous quadratic superpotential, providing new starting points for small W0 and phenomenology?

sources.title: Moduli potentials in string compactifications with fluxes: Mapping the discretuum

evidence.text: Can flux compactifications stabilize all moduli through F-terms while producing broken supersymmetry, a small nonnegative cosmological constant, and a hierarchy within weak coupling and large volume? Are the resulting vacua cosmologically viable?

sources.title: Searching the Landscape of Flux Vacua with Genetic Algorithms

evidence.text: Can genetic algorithms efficiently find type IIB flux vacua with prescribed string coupling, superpotential magnitude and moduli mass quantities, while revealing useful landscape structure?

sources.title: TASI Lectures on the Cosmological Constant

evidence.text: Can many moderately charged fluxes provide a dense vacuum spectrum while retaining large transition energies? The model separates closeness in vacuum energy from adjacency in the integer flux grid.

sources.title: Physics of String Flux Compactifications

evidence.text: How do fluxes stabilize compactification moduli and generate large vacuum ensembles, and what can statistical analysis of those ensembles say about cosmological constants, supersymmetry breaking, and the testability of string theory?

sources.title: Supersymmetry breaking and alpha-prime corrections to flux induced potentials

evidence.text: Which flux-induced M-theory vacua break supersymmetry while retaining zero three-dimensional cosmological constant and leading-order stability, and do perturbative α′ corrections destroy the corresponding no-scale structure in Type IIB compactifications?

sources.title: Smeared versus localised sources in flux compactifications

evidence.text: When do flux vacua constructed using smeared orientifolds or D-branes survive source localisation, and how does the answer depend on BPS relations and the resulting warping, dilaton and RR-field corrections?

sources.title: Applications of an exact counting formula in the Bousso-Polchinski Landscape

evidence.text: How can BP flux vacua be counted when the usual volume estimate fails, and what does improved counting imply for low-Λ abundances, typical flux occupation and estimates of the minimum nonnegative cosmological constant?

sources.title: Flux compactifications in string theory: A Comprehensive review

evidence.text: How do closed-string fluxes support four-dimensional type II vacua, constrain internal geometry, generate effective potentials and stabilize moduli? The review also examines corrections, proposed de Sitter constructions and statistical distributions of vacua.

sources.title: Computational Complexity of Vacua and Near-Vacua in Field and String Theory

evidence.text: What is the classical computational complexity of finding stable, metastable and approximate vacua, including the prior calculation of string-derived scalar potentials, and what conditional practical or cosmological consequences follow?

sources.title: TASI / PiTP / ISS lectures on moduli and microphysics

evidence.text: How do string-theoretic forces stabilize moduli and produce cosmological vacua, what microphysical degrees of freedom account for their entropy, and how do velocity-dependent effects change moduli dynamics?

sources.title: Distributions of nonsupersymmetric flux vacua

evidence.text: What determines the density and supersymmetry-breaking scale distribution of metastable nonsupersymmetric vacua in supergravity ensembles, especially Type IIB flux compactifications, and how do near-zero vacuum energy and additional D-type contributions change the result?

sources.title: Charting the landscape of N=4 flux compactifications

evidence.text: Which SO(3)-invariant vacua occur in isotropic Z2×Z2 flux compactifications with one set of sources, and which remain stable after including the full N=4 scalar spectrum?

sources.title: Topological Data Analysis for the String Landscape

evidence.text: Can persistent homology characterize multiscale structure in distributions of string vacua and reveal how restrictions on low-energy properties change that structure?

sources.title: Massive IIA flux compactifications and U-dualities

evidence.text: Do the DeWolfe et al. massive IIA orientifold vacua admit systematic large-flux low-energy or weak-string-coupling expansions once orientifold backreaction is included, and can dual descriptions clarify their dimensionality?

sources.title: Probing the Structure of String Theory Vacua with Genetic Algorithms and Reinforcement Learning

evidence.text: Can genetic algorithms and reinforcement learning efficiently find flux vacua with selected low-energy properties, reveal structure in their flux inputs, and make that structure more credible by comparing different sampling dynamics?

sources.title: Analytics of type IIB flux vacua and their mass spectra

evidence.text: Which type IIB flux configurations allow analytic axio-dilaton/complex-structure vacuum locations and mass spectra for arbitrarily many fields, and how do quadratic superpotentials and polynomial large-complex-structure corrections govern stabilization and flat directions?

sources.title: The Statistics of string / M theory vacua

evidence.text: Can estimates of the numbers and distributions of string/M vacua approximating the Standard Model clarify predictivity and falsifiability before identifying our vacuum?

sources.title: Chaotic coupling constants

evidence.text: Can finite-volume string moduli spaces and chaotic early-universe motion reduce initial-condition tuning in vacuum selection, and can conjectural S-duality constrain the nonperturbative potentials responsible for dilaton stabilization and supersymmetry breaking?

sources.title: Snowmass White Paper: String Theory and Particle Physics

evidence.text: How precisely can string vacua reproduce observed particle physics, which low-energy theories does quantum-gravity consistency exclude, and which Standard Model and beyond-Standard-Model features are typical or require tuning?

sources.title: Asymptotic Hodge Theory in String Compactifications and Integrable Systems

evidence.text: How can asymptotic Hodge theory characterize couplings and flux-vacuum loci in type IIB/F-theory compactifications, and construct solutions of certain two-dimensional integrable sigma models?

sources.title: Data analysis of millions of Type IIB flux vacua

evidence.text: What distributions, correlations and solution multiplicities occur in a large numerical scan of a two-complex-structure-modulus IIB flux model, and how effectively can flux representations predict numerical SUSY labels, potential values and moduli?

sources.title: Effective potentials, warping, and implications for F-term uplifting

evidence.text: How does non-ISD flux backreaction modify the off-shell Type IIB flux potential, and can complex-structure F-term uplifting remain controlled after warping and quantum corrections?

sources.title: Random polynomials and the friendly landscape

evidence.text: Can a friendly landscape, in which selected couplings scan while others remain sharply distributed, survive interactions among many moduli? What algebraic information about vacuum statistics can be extracted without solving every vacuum separately?

sources.title: Testing Swampland Conjectures with Machine Learning

evidence.text: How does selecting hierarchical flux configurations change the distribution of scalar-potential critical points relative to classified random flux configurations? Figure 8 compares Case A with Case B and retains four criterion or subclass labels.

sources.title: On the Flux Vacua in F-theory Compactifications

evidence.text: Can mirror-symmetry data including brane deformations produce F-theory flux vacua that stabilize all complex-structure fields near a large-complex-structure point?

sources.title: Asymmetric CFTs and GSUGRA

evidence.text: Do certain asymmetric conformal field theories describe the same vacua as fully backreacted gauged supergravities, thereby providing string realizations of non-geometric gaugings and partial supersymmetry breaking?

sources.title: Fixing moduli in exact type IIA flux vacua

evidence.text: Do the supersymmetric type IIA flux vacua obtained from four-dimensional effective theory admit ten-dimensional descriptions, how does flux/O6 backreaction modify Calabi–Yau geometry, and how does ten-dimensional flux quantization fix moduli?

sources.title: On the geometry of moduli space of polarized Calabi-Yau manifolds

evidence.text: The physical motivation is a previously derived asymptotic flux-vacuum counting formula involving a Weil-Petersson curvature integral. Its finiteness implications retain caveats from the cited counting work.

sources.title: Comments on Brane Recombination, Finite Flux Vacua, and the Swampland

evidence.text: This orientifold patch provides a concrete setting in which negative orientifold charge, magnetized brane charge and positive flux charge must balance. Its explicit brane families make the assumptions behind finite-vacua counting accessible to scrutiny.

sources.title: TASI Lectures on Remnants from the String Landscape

evidence.text: Could population and observer selection across many vacua explain some observed fine-tunings?

sources.title: Progress in D-brane model building

evidence.text: How can D-branes produce weakly coupled four-dimensional N=1 type II orientifold vacua with semi-realistic gauge sectors, and how do background fluxes change the allowed branes, effective couplings, moduli stabilization and supersymmetry breaking?

sources.title: Moduli stabilization from magnetic fluxes in type I string theory

evidence.text: Can quantized, constant open-string magnetic backgrounds stabilize Kähler and complex-structure moduli in four-dimensional supersymmetric type I vacua, with an exact string description and tunably large internal dimensions?

Do the DeWolfe et al. massive IIA orientifold vacua admit systematic large-flux low-energy or weak-string-coupling expansions once orientifold backreaction is included, and can dual descriptions clarify their dimensionality?

How do fluxes stabilize compactification moduli and generate large vacuum ensembles, and what can statistical analysis of those ensembles say about cosmological constants, supersymmetry breaking, and the testability of string theory?

Can finite-volume string moduli spaces and chaotic early-universe motion reduce initial-condition tuning in vacuum selection, and can conjectural S-duality constrain the nonperturbative potentials responsible for dilaton stabilization and supersymmetry breaking?

The physical motivation is a previously derived asymptotic flux-vacuum counting formula involving a Weil-Petersson curvature integral. Its finiteness implications retain caveats from the cited counting work.

evidence.text: How should field-space geometry, distance, and tower/species gradients be defined across equivalent conformal frames and choices of units? Which distance-conjecture bounds follow from frame covariance rather than specifically microscopic quantum gravity?

evidence.text: Can the gauge-versus-gravity proposal extend to higher-form fields and extended objects?

evidence.text: How can observed matter couplings coexist with a mesoscopic bulk dimension without diluting Standard Model interactions?

sources.title: Extra Dimensions and Physics of Low-Scale Strings

evidence.text: Why consider extra spatial dimensions, why might they remain hidden, and how could they manifest experimentally? This introductory review connects dimensional reduction, low fundamental scales, symmetry breaking and illustrative swampland conjectures.

sources.title: No U(1) ‘electric-magnetic’ duality in Einstein gravity

evidence.text: Does classical Einstein gravity admit a global U(1) analogue of Maxwell electric-magnetic duality beyond linear order, with curvature replacing field strength, and how can its failure in generic dynamics coexist with exact mass–NUT rotations in special solutions?

sources.title: Dark bubble cosmology and the equivalence principle

evidence.text: Does the bulk-field mechanism that gives abelian radiation the expected gravitational coupling in dark bubble cosmology also give Standard Model nonabelian sectors gravitational masses compatible with the weak equivalence principle?

sources.title: Introducing the Slotheon: a slow Galileon scalar field in curved space-time

evidence.text: Generalize flat Galilean shifts using covariantly constant Killing one-forms, inspect scalar equations using curvature contractions and Bianchi identities, and use existing second-order scalar-tensor classifications to restrict invariant operators.

sources.title: Small Vacuum Energy from Small Equivalence Violation in Scalar Gravity

evidence.text: The higher-dimensional treatment solves bulk equations and IR junction conditions perturbatively in backreaction, uses singular perturbation theory to match near-brane and slowly varying regions, and dimensionally reduces to a symmetry-constrained 5D EFT. Winding-loop potentials are estimated using large-argument Bessel asymptotics.

sources.title: DBI from Gravity

evidence.text: Act with Lie derivatives and exponentiated translations on a position-dependent metric family. Use Baker–Campbell–Hausdorff manipulations, a gravitational inverse Higgs relation, and projection onto localized modes to extract nonlinear transformations.

sources.title: Pseudotopological quasilocal energy of torsion gravity

evidence.text: Evaluate charges at infinity, impose falloffs, integrate the mass primitive, and choose a compatible reference. The fermionic application restricts variations to δa=0; integrability in that sector does not authorize changing the leading spinor coefficient.

sources.title: Signatures of extra dimensions in gravitational waves

evidence.text: Expand on an orthonormal basis of internal scalar-Laplacian eigenfunctions. Projection by integration extracts individual KK equations; integration over the compact manifold extracts the constant zero mode and removes total divergences.

sources.title: Euclidean wormholes, baby universes, and their impact on particle physics and cosmology

evidence.text: Derive the reparametrization constraint, reinterpret its solution as a field, and introduce interactions representing topology change. This supplies a dynamical alternative to simply integrating static α parameters.

sources.title: Global causality constraints in rotating scalar-tensor spacetimes

evidence.text: Can global chronology provide an additional consistency diagnostic for gravitational EFTs by testing whether a deformation moves circular closed timelike curves into a more accessible, EFT-controlled region than in the corresponding GR background?

sources.title: Non-equilibrium dynamics in Holography

evidence.text: How can a gravitational toy model represent strongly coupled fluids and crystals with broken translations? The source introduces a graviton mass sector while warning that generic choices can fail through instabilities invisible in linear analysis.

sources.title: Conformal and pure scale-invariant gravities in d dimensions

evidence.text: How do the background-dependent propagating modes of pure scale-invariant gravity and a particular conformal gravity generalize beyond four dimensions, and can alternative field frames simplify their analysis?

sources.title: Born-Infeld Gravity with a Unique Vacuum and a Massless Graviton

evidence.text: Can metric Born–Infeld gravity in n≥4 dimensions retain a unique viable maximally symmetric vacuum and only a unitary massless spin-2 excitation while including higher curvature terms?

sources.title: An Alternative to compactification

evidence.text: Can gravity appear four-dimensional with an infinite extra dimension and no Kaluza-Klein mass gap, through localization in a nonfactorizable background?

sources.title: A Note on Membrane Interactions and the Scalar potential

evidence.text: What forces follow from scalar, graviton and form-field exchange between identical extended sources? The model fixes the background dilaton, frame and source normalization before comparing exchange coefficients.

sources.title: Allowable complex scalars from Kaluza-Klein compactifications and metric rescalings

evidence.text: Which complex background metrics retain the matter convergence property used to define allowable geometries?

sources.title: Report of the Topical Group on Cosmic Probes of Fundamental Physics for for Snowmass 2021

evidence.text: Which observations can test spacetime symmetries, modified gravity, black-hole horizons and the quantum-gravity compatibility of low-energy EFTs?

sources.title: The Swampland Distance Conjecture and Towers of Tensionless Branes

evidence.text: What additional degrees of freedom appear when a scalar background approaches infinite proper distance in a gravitational theory?

sources.title: Dynamical tadpoles and Weak Gravity Constraints

evidence.text: Does an uncanceled source invalidate a theory or require its proposed background to evolve? The paper distinguishes propagating-field sources from compact-space charge constraints on nonpropagating forms.

sources.title: The Relation between physical and gravitational geometry

evidence.text: Within a two-geometry gravitational framework, how generally may the physical geometry governing matter differ from the gravitational metric? Can a Finsler physical geometry satisfy weak equivalence, causality, and consistency between particle and field descriptions?

sources.title: Logarithmic loop corrections, moduli stabilisation and de Sitter vacua in string theory

evidence.text: Could the special dimension in which the localized gravity term survives help select four noncompact spacetime dimensions? The paper proposes three orthogonal D7 sets whose transverse-volume stabilization accounts for the six compact directions.

sources.title: Snowmass White Paper: Implications of Quantum Gravity for Particle Physics

evidence.text: Review how quantum-gravity consistency conditions constrain low-energy EFT and might inform strong CP, the weak scale, new gauge interactions and dark energy. The white paper explicitly does not guarantee that gravitational considerations solve these problems.

sources.title: The String landscape and the swampland

evidence.text: Can the scalar target space of a gravitational low-energy theory have infinite metric volume? The initial setting isolates massless scalars with vanishing potential while permitting unspecified additional fields and higher-derivative corrections.

sources.title: How to deal with conformal and pure scale-invariant theories of gravity in d dimensions?

evidence.text: How do the propagating modes and ghost content change when pure scale-invariant and selected conformally invariant gravity theories are extended from four to d dimensions, and can changes of gravitational frame simplify their analysis?

sources.title: Isospectrality in Effective Field Theory Extensions of General Relativity

evidence.text: Can a nontrivial effective-field-theory extension of general relativity preserve polarization-independent gravitational-wave propagation and black-hole quasinormal-mode isospectrality, at least in the eikonal limit?

sources.title: The UV fate of anomalous U(1)s and the Swampland

evidence.text: How does a mixed gravitational anomaly change the light-vector hierarchy? The taxicab spectrum isolates this effect with an exactly vanishing cubic trace.

sources.title: Approximate Symmetries and Gravity

evidence.text: How small can explicit global-symmetry violation become in an EFT coupled to gravity, and what additional states or validity limits prevent an exact-symmetry limit?

sources.title: Two scalar fields inflation from scale-invariant gravity with modified measure

evidence.text: Can globally scale-invariant gravity with an independent integration measure naturally generate two scalar degrees of freedom, inflation and a small positive final vacuum energy in the second-order formalism?

sources.title: Speed of gravity

evidence.text: How do higher-curvature corrections in the EFT of GR change gravitational-wave propagation relative to minimally coupled matter on backgrounds that spontaneously break Lorentz invariance, and what can positivity and causality imply about the sign?

sources.title: Emergence of Weak Coupling at Large Distance in Quantum Gravity

evidence.text: What restrictions does quantum gravity impose on continuous parameters and asymptotic scalar-field geometry? The imported conjectures connect scalar expectation values, infinite moduli-space diameter, and towers becoming exponentially light with geodesic distance.
